findings.old:

findings.new: 'llmsx[tui] @ https://llmsx.org/downloads/llmsx/${wheel}'

findings.finding: Zero-telemetry claim covers external runners without evidence.
findings.old: Zero credentials required to browse. Zero telemetry. All notes and highlights persist locally on your machine.
findings.new: Browsing needs no model credential. Notes and highlights are stored locally; configured research runners may contact their provider.

findings.finding: Frontier proposals do not establish complete research boundaries.
findings.old:
Browse hundreds of researched concepts organized in a coherent taxonomy. Frontier concepts
        (unexplored boundaries) are rendered dim-italic, revealing the exact edges of your current
        knowledge base.
findings.new: Browse mapped topics and published references in the concept tree. Frontier names appear dim and italic; they record proposed gaps, not proof of the map’s complete boundaries.

findings.finding: Generated quiz explanations are not verification.
findings.old: Explanations verify subtle mechanical distinctions.
findings.new: Explanations describe distinctions to check against the source material.

findings.finding: Research runner launch does not guarantee exhaustive work.
findings.old:
Exhausts one concept depth-first. Traverses underlying
        dependencies, edge cases, and architectural mechanisms to build an exhaustive technical dossier.
findings.new: Studies one concept depth-first, including dependencies, edge cases and architectural mechanisms, within the skill’s scope and stopping conditions.

findings.finding: Not every local model supports required tools and research may fetch sources.
findings.old: Zero-cloud offline execution with any local model
findings.new: Model inference through a configured local model

findings.finding: Missing runner and source-fetch prerequisites.
findings.old: Optional OLLAMA_API_KEY for remote instances.
findings.new: Optional OLLAMA_API_KEY for remote instances. Ollama research also requires Claude Code; research tools may need internet access.

findings.finding: Tree-file restore is not repository-wide recovery.
findings.old: tree snapshot is atomically restored. Your repo is never left in a corrupted state.
findings.new: tree snapshot is restored atomically. This protects the tree file; it does not roll back every file a runner may change.

findings.finding: Source-linked facts are not automatically verified.
findings.old: its primary definition, verified facts, and architectural
findings.new: its primary definition, source-linked facts, and architectural

findings.finding: Site host is Cloudflare Pages.
findings.old: Hosted publicly on GitHub Pages / CDN
findings.new: Published website on Cloudflare Pages

findings.finding: Explorer summary still promises unconditional failed-run rollback.
findings.old: If a job fails or cancels, tree snapshots are restored atomically.
findings.new: Timeouts and cancellations restore the tree snapshot; other failures validate the tree and restore it only if invalid.

findings.finding: Only tree snapshot exists; valid failed-run changes survive.
findings.old:
Before any research runner touches the repo, a git and
      tree snapshot is recorded. If a job crashes, times out, or is cancelled (<kbd>x</kbd>), the
      tree snapshot is restored atomically. This protects the tree file; it does not roll back every file a runner may change.
findings.new: Before a research job starts, the explorer snapshots the tree file. Timeouts and cancellations (<kbd>x</kbd>) restore it. Other completed runs, including runners that report an error, restore it only if validation finds an unreadable or structurally invalid tree. Review the diff after a failed run; valid tree changes and changes to other files can remain.

findings.finding: Web concept tree exposes authenticated moderator research, not only read-only views.
findings.old: Read-only generated views
findings.new: Public generated browsing; signed-in moderators can request research

findings.finding: Comparison should state terminal configuration requirement rather than imply all runners always available.
findings.source: llmsx/llmsx/explorer.py job dispatch and explorer_store.py provider configuration
findings.old: Live multi-engine /dr, queue, & background execution
findings.new: Locally configured research runners, queue and background jobs

    calls on indexing, and the wall time of a job that holds a worker. Retrieval

Tracking usage does not by itself mean a dollar charge. Quotas belong to the plan, not the page.

findings.finding: Existing-index retrieval is metered for usage/quota even when keyword calls are not billable.
findings.old:
Three things: model tokens on the refine and vocabulary passes, embedding
    calls on indexing, and the wall time of a job that holds a worker. Retrieval
    against an already-built index is not metered, which is why the keyword leg
    of a hybrid query costs nothing at all. The quota thresholds themselves are
    per plan, not per page.
findings.new: Usage entries can record model tokens, embedding calls and job wall time. Query usage is tracked too: hosted keyword retrieval counts against the account’s query quota but is not billable. Semantic and hybrid retrieval follow separate plan permissions and billing rules; the current free plan limits semantic search to the fixed demo. Tracking usage does not by itself mean a dollar charge. Quotas belong to the plan, not the page.
